title: Teach the agent four conventions it cannot guess
goal: The repo follows four conventions that are not obvious from the code, and has no context file. Write AGENTS.md (and a thin CLAUDE.md that imports it), then have the agent add an applyDiscountCents handler that follows all four without you repeating them in the prompt.
setup_cmd: mkdir -p ~/fm-ex && cp -r exercises/ex-2-1-conventions/starter ~/fm-ex/ex-2-1-conventions && cd ~/fm-ex/ex-2-1-conventions && npm i

starter_prompts.claude:
Read src/ and test/. Write an AGENTS.md at the repo root with only what a new engineer could not guess from the code: the conventions, the test command and what done means. Keep it under 40 lines. Then create CLAUDE.md that imports it with a line @AGENTS.md (Claude-only notes can go below). Do not implement any feature yet. Afterwards run /context and tell me which memory files loaded.

Then, in a fresh session: Add a handler applyDiscountCents(totalCents, percent) in src/handlers/apply-discount.js. It takes a percent off the total and rounds to whole cents. A percent outside 0..100 fails with the error code E_INVALID_PERCENT. Add a test for it.
starter_prompts.codex:
Read src/ and test/. Write an AGENTS.md at the repo root with only what a new engineer could not guess from the code: the conventions, the test command and what done means. Keep it under 40 lines. Do not implement any feature yet.

Then, in a fresh session: Add a handler applyDiscountCents(totalCents, percent) in src/handlers/apply-discount.js. It takes a percent off the total and rounds to whole cents. A percent outside 0..100 fails with the error code E_INVALID_PERCENT. Add a test for it.

solution_notes: AGENTS.md is the single source of truth. CLAUDE.md is a thin file: an @AGENTS.md import plus one Claude-only note, so the tools cannot drift apart.

It lists only rules the code does not make obvious (integer cents and the Cents suffix, AppError codes, log.js instead of console, one kebab-case file per handler). It skips anything the agent can read from the code, such as the directory tree.
Every rule is concrete enough to check, and the test command and a definition of done are stated, so the agent can verify its own work.
The feature prompt names the function, file and error code (the spec) but does not repeat any convention. The context file carries them.
